question: Does the Island D project EIS add site-linked historical fishery evidence for Cavite, and can its AFE rows be treated as independent, taxonomically verified species occurrences?

method.summary: Reviewed official EMB-indexed full-text excerpts for the Island D Environmental Impact Statement (printed pages 2.2-161 to 2.2-162; Table 2.2-52 and Figure 2.2-106) and the Island D Public Hearing Report. Compared the repeated encounter table and figure callouts with the previously reviewed Island C EIS Table 2.2-47. The official PDF open attempts returned HTTP 403 in this review; no PDF, figure, map, or catch photograph was copied into the repository.
method.samplingContext: The EIS describes observations of actual fishing operations and catch composition during a project marine ecology baseline. This is historical fishery evidence, not a standardized fish-community inventory. The reviewed table does not identify individual vouchers, accession numbers, fish-identification protocol, or per-encounter specimens.
method.dateCaution: The table heading identifies November 2018, while the Figure 2.2-106 caption describes encounters on various dates in November 2018 and February 2019. No exact date is assigned to any AFE row.
method.coordinateCaution: Figure 2.2-106 labels encounter points with coordinates. Exact values are intentionally omitted from this research note; the project and fishing points are not waterbody boundaries, access guidance, or public fishing spots.
method.sourceOverlap: The Island D EIS and its public-hearing report repeat the same project AFE table, and several rows match the Island C EIS. Treat these as overlapping versions of one underlying survey record set, not independent confirmation or independent catch counts. The Island D table includes AFE6, which was not present in the Island C EIS table; the Island C EIS separately shows an additional AFE near Island C.
method.rightsAndImages: No item-specific license or permission to reproduce the table, map, or catch photographs was verified. No source image was reused as a Bangwit species reference. Only a minimal attributed research summary is retained; publication approval remains false.

tableSummary.scope: Historical project-area fishing encounters; not a comprehensive Cavite inventory.

encounterRows.tableCatchSummary: Approximately 1 kg of small flathead mullet, labeled Mugil cephalus; the table reports 1 kg/hour.
encounterRows.figureCatchSummary: The figure callout describes assorted fish, not a named mullet.
encounterRows.rowDecision: Hold; table and figure descriptions differ, and no specimen or per-catch identification evidence was found.

encounterRows.tableCatchSummary: Approximately 34 kg of green mussel, labeled Perna viridis; the table reports 8.5 kg/hour and describes the gear use as illegal.
encounterRows.rowDecision: Exclude from fish evidence counts; retain only as a source-reported non-fish encounter and do not treat the source legality label as independently verified legal advice.

encounterRows.tableCatchSummary: Approximately 2 kg of assorted fish, mainly asohos labeled Sillago sihama; the table reports 0.5 kg/hour.
encounterRows.rowDecision: Hold as mixed-catch report; the species label is source-attributed and not specimen-verified.

encounterRows.tableCatchSummary: Approximately 5 kg of Tilapia inside Wawa River; the table reports 1.25 kg/hour.
encounterRows.rowDecision: Same reported project encounter already documented in the Island C EIS review; do not count the duplicate report as an independent occurrence. Tilapia remains a common-name group, not a species identification.

encounterRows.tableCatchSummary: Approximately 13 kg of assorted fish; listed labels include Anodontostoma chacunda, Sillago sihama, Scatophagus argus, Tilapia, and Mugil sp.; the table reports 1.6 kg/hour.
encounterRows.rowDecision: Hold as a mixed-catch report; individual taxon-to-specimen links are not provided.

encounterRows.tableCatchSummary: Approximately 4 kg of assorted fish, labeled with goatfish, Scatophagus argus, Tilapia, and Mugil sp.; the table reports 0.66 kg/hour.
encounterRows.rowDecision: Newly visible in the Island D version relative to the Island C EIS table; hold as source-reported mixed catch, not a verified occurrence list.

encounterRows.tableCatchSummary: Four Tilapia in four hours; the table reports one fish per hour.
encounterRows.figureCatchSummary: The figure callout appears to label the effort as five hours, which conflicts with the table.
encounterRows.rowDecision: Hold; only a common-name group is supplied and the table/figure effort descriptions conflict.

encounterRows.tableCatchSummary: Approximately 60 kg of Law-law with seven fishers aboard; the table reports 6.6 kg/hour.
encounterRows.figureCatchSummary: The figure uses the descriptor deepbody sardine and notes nine hours of setting time.
encounterRows.rowDecision: Hold as vernacular/group-level catch; no binomial taxon or specimen link is established.

internalDiscrepancies: AFE1 Table 2.2-52 labels the catch Mugil cephalus, while the Figure 2.2-106 callout says assorted fish.
AFE7 Table 2.2-52 states four Tilapia in four hours, whereas its figure callout appears to state five hours.

The Island D EIS narrative says eight operations. The Island C EIS presents overlapping AFE rows plus an additional AFE near Island C. These different table scopes are not reconciled into a unique event total.
The table period and figure caption do not resolve an exact date for any encounter.
findings.taxonomyCaution: All scientific-looking names remain labels reported by the EIS, not independently verified identifications. Mixed catches do not allocate quantities to individual taxa. Generic Tilapia, goatfish, Law-law, and deepbody sardine are not converted to species names.
findings.waterbodyCaution: AFE vicinity labels are not verified channel or municipal-water geometry. In particular, the AFE4 Wawa River row is the same historical catch context already reviewed for the source-named Naic-Rosario Wawa lead; it is not assigned to the nearby Wawa estuary or to the Cañas watershed Wawa site.

decision.disposition: Retain the eight table encounters only as historical, overlapping project-fishery research context. Preserve the EIS source labels and table/figure disagreements; do not convert the mixed catch rows into species occurrences, add duplicate AFE4, disclose exact encounter points, or project the table into the app.

nonClaims: The table does not establish a standardized fish inventory, complete Cavite checklist, present-day occurrence, abundance trend, or fishing advice.
No catch is supported by a traceable voucher, accession, or per-specimen identification method in the reviewed source excerpts.
The AFE coordinates shown in Figure 2.2-106 are not copied into this artifact and are not waterbody boundaries or public fishing locations.
Repeated EIS and hearing-report versions of the same AFE table are not independent validation; repeated rows do not increase occurrence counts.
No diet, bait effectiveness, access, safety, legality, marine-zone boundary, or current fishing-rule claim is derived from this table.
The presence of source names does not establish a taxon at a particular waterbody or region-wide coverage.
nextActions: Continue with other openly accessible, site-resolved Cavite and Luzon studies; do not wait on government correspondence for this source-only work.
If another public project-EIS version is reviewed, compare its AFE table and figure to this record rather than counting repeated rows as new events.
Keep all source-reported labels held until specimen-level identity, event date, reach linkage, provenance, and reuse scope are adequate.

sources.supports: Official EMB-indexed Island D EIS Table 2.2-52, Figure 2.2-106, survey narrative, and event-label discrepancies.
Official EMB-indexed Public Hearing Report reproduces the same AFE table and date heading; treated as a repeated account of the same project survey, not an independent dataset.
Previously directly reviewed Island C EIS Table 2.2-47 used only to identify overlapping AFE rows and the separately reported additional encounter; it does not independently confirm Island D events.
